text: Trial-and-error rulemaking is suboptimal because participating actors acquire the necessary information ex-post, only after rules have turned out to be suboptimal, rather than increasing the availability of relevant information ex-ante.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

isBasedOn.name: Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework

abstract: is suboptimal for rulemaking because, rather than increasing the availability of relevant information ex-ante (through a dynamic process as proposed in this paper), participating actors acquire the necessary information ex-post after rules turn out to be suboptimal.
